topic: Alcohol withdrawal syndrome and delirium tremens management in ICU
scope: Stored full NICE CG100 text on acute alcohol withdrawal, delirium tremens, and withdrawal seizures in hospital.

keyRecommendations.text: Offer hospital admission for medically assisted withdrawal if the person has, or is at high risk of, withdrawal seizures or delirium tremens.
Use a symptom-triggered regimen in hospital or where 24-hour assessment is available.
For delirium tremens, offer oral lorazepam first. If symptoms persist or oral medication is declined, offer parenteral lorazepam or haloperidol. Do not offer phenytoin for withdrawal seizures.

clinicalBottomLine: Admit high-risk withdrawal, including delirium tremens and seizures, for medically assisted withdrawal; treat delirium tremens with oral lorazepam first and do not use phenytoin for withdrawal seizures.
notableCaveats: CG100 is hospital guidance and does not set ICU ventilator targets. MCQs stay inside the withdrawal, delirium tremens, and seizure recommendations.

source.title: Alcohol-use disorders: diagnosis and management of physical complications. NICE guideline CG100.
